newsitem.title: DUBAI: First export of new Qatar crude set for November.
newsitem.headline: First export of new Qatar crude set for November.

text.p: The first cargo of Qatar's new Al-Rayyan crude grade is scheduled to be exported in early November, the offshore field operator said on Wednesday.

"The best estimate is production at Al-Rayyan will start in early October...the first cargo will be ready in the first week of November," Paul Fronterhouse, vice president and resident manager of Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) in Qatar said.
Al-Rayyan output will be gradually increased to a full rate of 35,000 barrels per day (bpd) after start up, adding to OPEC member Qatar's current estimated total output of 480,000 bpd.
The 25 API gravity Al-Rayyan crude will be sold separately from Qatar's main Qatar Land and Marine export grades, with the Far East seen as the primary market for the crude.
"It will fit best in the Far East market but we are actively pursuing opportunities to sell in Europe and the west coast of the U.S.," Fronterhouse said.

ARCO, together with foreign shareholders in the field and the state-owned Qatar General Petroleum Corp, will market the crude and sales are expected to priced in relation to Saudi Arabia's Arab Heavy grade, he said.

Al-Rayyan oil will be sold in cargoes of between 500,000 barrels and 600,000 barrels with supplies delivered from the 900,000 barrels capacity Ailsa Craig ship which acts as an offshore storage facility.
The storage ship has the capacity to handle Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) of about two million barrels which would allow potential customers to load Al-Rayyan with other Gulf crudes.

First production at the Al-Rayyan field was originally scheduled for September, though this has been delayed. The field's platform is expected to leave Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates on September 14 for the site and it will take three weeks before it is installed and production starts.

ARCO Qatar Inc, operator of the Al-Rayyan field, has a 27.5 percent stake in a consortium with Gulfstream Resources Canada Ltd (also 27.5 percent), British Gas Plc (25 percent, and the German firms Wintershall (15 percent) and Preussag Energie (5.0 percent).
